key_insight: For Alzheimer’s caregivers, traditional machine learning worked best when wearable data and interview text were combined, while LLMs performed better on interview text alone.
clinical_relevance: This suggests multimodal screening tools could help flag caregivers at higher psychological risk earlier, especially for stress, burden, and loneliness.
method: Compared wearable-derived features, interview-based text, and combined multimodal inputs.
Classified risk using the Perceived Stress Scale, Zarit Burden Interview, and UCLA Loneliness Scale.
Benchmarked traditional machine learning against Gemini 2.0, Llama 4, and GPT-4o with different prompting strategies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that model performance varied by modality, with traditional ML strongest in multimodal settings and LLMs strongest for interview-only input, and that PSS was the most predictable construct.
watch_item: Performance depended heavily on prompting and input type, so results may not generalize without careful validation in new caregiver populations and settings.
paper_title: Wearable and Interview-based Assessment of Psychological Risk in Alzheimers Caregivers: Machine Learning vs. Large Language Models
